title: Organic Molecules
seo_title: Grade 12 Physical Sciences: Organic Molecules Worksheets (CAPS)
standard_text: Organic molecular structures: functional groups, homologous series (alkanes, alkenes, alkynes, haloalkanes, alcohols, aldehydes, ketones, carboxylic acids, esters); IUPAC naming and formulae; structural isomers; physical properties and intermolecular forces; reactions: combustion, esterification, substitution, addition and elimination; plastics and polymers. (summary of CAPS Physical Sciences, Grade 12, Chemistry: Organic molecules)
meta_desc: Free Grade 12 Physical Sciences worksheets (CAPS): functional groups, IUPAC names, isomers, physical properties, organic reactions and polymers. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A homologous series has the same functional group and general formula.
body_html:
How to think about it

Organic compounds contain carbon. Each homologous series has a functional group: C=C (alkenes), –OH (alcohols), –CHO (aldehydes), C=O in the chain (ketones), –COOH (carboxylic acids), –COO– (esters). IUPAC names use the longest chain (meth-, eth-, prop-, but-, pent-) and the suffix of the functional group.

Boiling points increase with chain length (stronger London forces) and are higher for alcohols and acids (hydrogen bonds). Alkanes undergo substitution with halogens; alkenes undergo addition (hydrogenation, hydration, halogenation); elimination makes alkenes. An alcohol and a carboxylic acid form an ester. Addition polymers such as polythene are made from alkenes.

Example

Name CH₃CH₂CH₂OH.

3 carbons, –OH on C1

Answer: propan-1-ol

Example

Ethanol + ethanoic acid → ?

Esterification

Answer: ethyl ethanoate + water

Common mistakes

  • Numbering the chain from the wrong end.
  • Thinking alkenes undergo substitution.
  • Mixing up aldehydes and ketones.

faq.q: Why does butane boil at a higher temperature than propane?
faq.a: It is a longer molecule with stronger London forces.

faq.q: Why are plastics a problem for the environment?
faq.a: Most are not biodegradable, so they last for hundreds of years in landfills and oceans.

items.q: Which compound has the formula C₃H₈?
items.e: Count the carbon atoms (3: prop-) and look at the functional group.

items.q: What is the molecular formula of the alkane with 20 carbon atoms?
items.e: Alkanes are C<sub>n</sub>H<sub>2n+2</sub>.

items.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH(Cl)CH<sub>3</sub>?
items.e: The longest chain has 4 carbons (but-). Number from the end that gives the lowest locant.

items.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH=CHCH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>3</sub>?
items.e: The longest chain has 6 carbons (hex-). Number from the end that gives the lowest locant.

items.q: Which alkane forms when 1-bromopropane reacts with sodium in dry ether (Wurtz reaction)?
items.e: Two alkyl groups join: 2R–X + 2Na → R–R. A C3 group gives hexane.

items.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH(Br)CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>3</sub>?
items.e: The longest chain has 5 carbons (pent-). Number from the end that gives the lowest locant.

items.e: Propene has 3 carbon atoms (prop-). Alkenes are CₙH₂ₙ.

items.q: What is the molecular formula of ethanol?
items.e: Ethanol has 2 carbon atoms (eth-). Alcohols are CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH.

items.q: Which alkane forms when bromomethane reacts with sodium in dry ether (Wurtz reaction)?
items.e: Two alkyl groups join: 2R–X + 2Na → R–R. A C1 group gives ethane.

items.q: What is the molecular formula of propane?

items.q: Which functional group is found in an amide?
items.e: –CONH₂ is the functional group of an amide.

items.q: How many moles of oxygen are needed to burn one mole of C<sub>4</sub>H<sub>10</sub> completely?
items.e: C<sub>n</sub>H<sub>2n+2</sub> + (3n+1)/2 O<sub>2</sub> → nCO<sub>2</sub> + (n+1)H<sub>2</sub>O. 4 CO₂ need 8 O atoms, 5 H₂O need 5 O atoms: 13 ÷ 2 = 6½.

items.q: Which functional group is found in a carboxylic acid?
items.e: –COOH is the functional group of a carboxylic acid.

items.q: Which class of compound has the functional group –NH₂?
items.e: –NH₂ is the functional group of an amine.

items.q: What is the molecular formula of the alkene with 7 carbon atoms and one C=C bond?
items.e: Alkenes are C<sub>n</sub>H<sub>2n</sub>.

items.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH<sub>2</sub>BrCH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>3</sub>?
items.e: The longest chain has 3 carbons (prop-). Number from the end that gives the lowest locant.

items.q: Which functional group is found in a ketone?
items.e: –CO– (between two carbons) is the functional group of a ketone.

items.q: Which class of compound has the functional group –CO– (between two carbons)?
items.e: –CO– (between two carbons) is the functional group of a ketone.

items.q: Which reagent distinguishes an aldehyde from a ketone?
c: Tollens' reagent (silver mirror with the aldehyde)
items.e: Aldehydes are oxidised; ketones are not.

items.q: What is the catalyst for making an ester from an alcohol and a carboxylic acid?
items.e: The reaction is reversible and slow without it.

items.q: Pentyl butanoate is hydrolysed. Which acid and alcohol form?
items.e: Split at the C–O bond: the -oate part gives the acid, the -yl part gives the alcohol.

items.q: What mechanism happens when HCN (from KCN and acid) reacts with ethanal?
items.e: CN⁻ attacks the δ+ carbonyl carbon.

items.q: What links the amino acids in a protein?
items.e: Formed by condensation, losing water.

items.q: What is the name of the ester made from pentanoic acid and propan-1-ol?
items.e: The alcohol part is named first (propyl), then the acid part (pentanoate).

items.q: Why does the product of HCN adding to ethanal form a racemic mixture?
c: CN⁻ can attack the planar carbonyl from either side equally
the product has no chiral carbon
items.e: Equal amounts of both enantiomers form.

items.q: What type of polymer is nylon-6,6?
items.e: Made from a diamine and a dicarboxylic acid with loss of water.

items.q: Which compound gives a positive iodoform test?
items.e: It has a CH₃CO– group.

items.q: Why is benzene less reactive than cyclohexene towards bromine?
c: its delocalised electrons are spread out, so the electron density is lower
items.e: Benzene needs a halogen carrier such as FeBr₃.

items.q: Why is phenylamine a weaker base than ethylamine?
c: the nitrogen lone pair is delocalised into the benzene ring
items.e: The lone pair is less available to accept a proton.

items.q: Which reagent reduces nitrobenzene to phenylamine?
items.e: Followed by adding NaOH.

items.q: What is the product when ethanoyl chloride reacts with ammonia?
items.e: Addition–elimination gives an amide.

items.q: What is formed when an aldehyde is reduced with NaBH₄?
items.e: H⁻ (hydride) attacks the carbonyl carbon.

items.q: Why are polyesters biodegradable while polyalkenes are not?
c: their ester links can be hydrolysed
items.e: Polyalkenes have only non-polar C–C and C–H bonds.

items.q: What is the zwitterion of an amino acid?
c: an ion with both a positive (NH₃⁺) and a negative (COO⁻) group
items.e: Found at the isoelectric point.

items.q: What is used to give a coloured spot for amino acids in chromatography?
items.e: Amino acids are colourless.

items.q: Why does benzene react by substitution rather than addition?
c: substitution keeps the stable delocalised ring of electrons
benzene is not reactive at all
items.e: The delocalised π system gives extra stability.

items.q: What gas forms when a carboxylic acid reacts with sodium carbonate?
items.e: This fizzing is a test for carboxylic acids.

items.q: Why are aldehydes more reactive than ketones in nucleophilic addition?
c: they have less steric hindrance and less electron release to the carbonyl carbon
items.e: Ketones have two alkyl groups.

items.q: How many structural isomers does C₄H₁₀ have?
items.e: Butane and methylpropane.

items.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH<sub>3</sub>CH(CH<sub>3</sub>)CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>3</sub>?
items.e: The longest chain has 4 carbons (but-). Number from the end that gives the lowest locant.

items.q: What is the name of the ester made from ethanoic acid and pentan-1-ol?
items.e: The alcohol part is named first (pentyl), then the acid part (ethanoate).

items.q: What is the name of the ester made from pentanoic acid and butan-1-ol?
items.e: The alcohol part is named first (butyl), then the acid part (pentanoate).

items.q: What is formed when an aldehyde reacts with hydroxylamine?
items.e: C=N–OH.

items.q: What is the molecular formula of the alkene with 19 carbon atoms and one C=C bond?
items.e: Alkenes are C<sub>n</sub>H<sub>2n</sub>.

items.q: Propyl methanoate is hydrolysed. Which acid and alcohol form?
items.e: Split at the C–O bond: the -oate part gives the acid, the -yl part gives the alcohol.

items.q: What type of mechanism happens when bromoethane reacts with aqueous NaOH?
items.e: OH⁻ attacks the δ+ carbon.

items.q: Why are CFCs harmful to the ozone layer?
c: UV light makes chlorine radicals that break down ozone
items.e: One Cl• can destroy thousands of O₃ molecules.

items.q: Which pollutant forms from incomplete combustion?
items.e: Not enough oxygen gives CO and soot.

items.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH<sub>3</sub>CH(Br)CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>3</sub>?
items.e: The longest chain has 5 carbons (pent-). Number from the end that gives the lowest locant.

items.q: What type of mechanism happens when bromine reacts with ethene?
items.e: The C=C bond is electron-rich and attracts electrophiles.

items.q: Why are addition polymers like poly(propene) hard to dispose of?
c: they are unreactive and not biodegradable
items.e: They are saturated with strong non-polar bonds.

items.q: What forms when 1-bromopropane is warmed with excess ethanolic ammonia?
items.e: NH₃ acts as a nucleophile; excess limits further substitution.

items.q: Methyl propanoate is hydrolysed. Which acid and alcohol form?
items.e: Split at the C–O bond: the -oate part gives the acid, the -yl part gives the alcohol.

items.q: Why is the C–I bond the most reactive carbon–halogen bond?
c: it has the lowest bond enthalpy
items.e: Bond strength matters more than polarity.

items.q: Why do primary amines have higher boiling points than tertiary amines of similar mass?
c: primary amines form hydrogen bonds; tertiary amines cannot
items.e: Tertiary amines have no N–H.

items.q: Which amine does not react with benzenesulphonyl chloride (Hinsberg)?
items.e: It has no N–H hydrogen.

items.q: What is the molecular formula of the alkene with 15 carbon atoms and one C=C bond?
items.e: Alkenes are C<sub>n</sub>H<sub>2n</sub>.

items.q: How many structural isomers does C₅H₁₂ have?
items.e: Pentane, 2-methylbutane and 2,2-dimethylpropane.

items.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH(Br)CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>3</sub>?
items.e: The longest chain has 6 carbons (hex-). Number from the end that gives the lowest locant.

items.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH<sub>3</sub>CH=CHCH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>3</sub>?
items.e: The longest chain has 6 carbons (hex-). Number from the end that gives the lowest locant.

items.q: What is the monomer of poly(ethene)?
items.e: Remove “poly” and the brackets to find the monomer.

items.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>Br?
items.e: The longest chain has 5 carbons (pent-). Number from the end that gives the lowest locant.

items.q: Which ester is made when methanoic acid reacts with ethanol?
items.e: The alcohol gives the first part (ethyl) and the acid gives the second part (methanoate). Water is also made.

items.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH<sub>3</sub>CH(OH)CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>3</sub>?
items.e: The longest chain has 5 carbons (pent-). Number from the end that gives the lowest locant.

items.q: What is the monomer of poly(tetrafluoroethene) (PTFE)?
items.e: Remove “poly” and the brackets to find the monomer.

items.q: What colour change is seen when acidified potassium dichromate oxidises an alcohol?
items.e: Cr₂O₇²⁻ is reduced to Cr³⁺.

items.q: Which polymer is used for water pipes and cable insulation?
items.e: Poly(chloroethene) (PVC): water pipes and cable insulation.

items.q: What is the molecular formula of the alkene with 17 carbon atoms and one C=C bond?
items.e: Alkenes are C<sub>n</sub>H<sub>2n</sub>.

items.q: Which method purifies camphor or naphthalene?
items.e: They change directly from solid to vapour.

items.q: Which type of isomerism do propan-1-ol and propan-2-ol show?
items.e: The –OH is on a different carbon.

items.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>OH?
items.e: The longest chain has 3 carbons (prop-). Number from the end that gives the lowest locant.

items.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH(Br)CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>3</sub>?
items.e: The longest chain has 6 carbons (hex-). Number from the end that gives the lowest locant.

items.q: Which two compounds react to make ethyl methanoate?
items.e: Ethyl- comes from ethanol; -methanoate comes from methanoic acid.

items.q: Which ester is made when ethanoic acid reacts with ethanol?
items.e: The alcohol gives the first part (ethyl) and the acid gives the second part (ethanoate). Water is also made.

items.q: Which ester is made when methanoic acid reacts with butanol?
items.e: The alcohol gives the first part (butyl) and the acid gives the second part (methanoate). Water is also made.

items.q: Which addition polymer is made from the monomer propene?
items.e: Put “poly” and brackets around the monomer name.

items.q: What is heterolytic cleavage?
c: a bond breaks so one atom keeps both electrons, giving ions
items.e: Shown with full curved arrows.

items.q: What is the repeating unit of poly(ethene)?
items.e: The C=C opens up to join the monomers.
